explanation: In C++, function templates enable writing generic functions that can operate on different data types without rewriting code for each type. When combined with custom predicates (function objects, lambdas, or function pointers), they allow flexible, type-agnostic algorithms that can be customized for specific comparison or matching criteria. This approach promotes code reuse, type safety, and adaptability in generic programming, especially within the Standard Template Library (STL).
syntax:
template <typename InputIterator1, typename InputIterator2, typename BinaryPredicate>
std::pair<InputIterator1, InputIterator2> mismatch(InputIterator1 first1, InputIterator1 last1,
                                                    InputIterator2 first2, InputIterator2 last2,
                                                    BinaryPredicate pred);
example_explanation: This example demonstrates a function template 'find_end' that searches for the last occurrence of a sequence within a range, using a custom predicate defined as a lambda. The predicate compares elements for equality. The code shows how to invoke the template with specific iterators and a predicate, illustrating the flexibility of template functions combined with user-defined comparison logic in modern C++.
